motivation: The two initial native comparisons measured approximately 240 additional retained bytes per used/active Actor. Shared refresh and capped-grant costs also increased; those observations remain retained rather than replaced.
candidate: Replace the eagerly allocated per-runtime WeakSet with a current-owner record and a lazily allocated ancestor array. Ordinary nonnested ticks create no guard collection. Release ancestor storage after the outer call, including failures.
preserved: Reject same-owner advance before the empty-map return.
Allow another owner and reject every still-active ancestor.
Restore the enclosing owner after nested success or failure.
Permit an unwound owner while an outer call remains active.
Keep the exact 64-operation nesting bound and partial-commit semantics.
Keep supplied-port snapshots, validation and native publication/cue behavior.
Retain no owner references after the outer operation returns or throws.
tradeoffsAndLimits: Ancestor lookup is linear in the active nesting depth, bounded to 63 ancestors; the native benchmark does not time deeply nested callback chains.
Cross-owner nesting allocates temporary ancestor storage. Retained-heap measurements do not quantify allocation volume or peak memory.
The memory benchmark measures warmed Actor graphs after grants/removal. The separate collection test covers ordinary, nested and failed timer updates, without a byte-budget claim for those paths.
CPU profiling identified costs across adapter/runtime/stat work rather than one removable operation. Grant validation and publication remain unchanged in this candidate.
No improvement is accepted before the prescribed comparisons. Desktop results do not establish Steam Deck, mobile or native-engine performance.
